title: Landing Party — Upgrade Options
summary: Commander Spock pays off land names: whenever he enters or attacks he reveals the top card, lets you cast it for free if its mana value is at most the number of differently named lands you control, puts it onto the battlefield if it's a land, and otherwise draws it. The stock list ramps, lands 35 different names and already carries six blink and copy effects that make Spock enter again (Chief Kyle, Temporal Tribulation, The Guardian of Forever, Balance of Terror, Colossal Clone Master, Shore Leave Planet), but it has only three real answers and fires its ten landfall payoffs off a single extra land drop. Each direction buys four shared answers plus one engine of six cards, and every direction keeps the blink pieces the precon built around Spock.

notes: Curve is high: 59 nonland cards besides Spock at an average MV of 3.58, with ten at six mana or more (eight at six, Lt. Arex at seven, Planet Killer at eight).

Spock's free-cast ceiling is the number of differently named lands on the battlefield — 35 names across 40 lands, but 4 Forest, 2 Island and 2 Plains mean those 40 cards only ever count as 35, and the ceiling creeps up one name at a time.
Only three cards answer a resolved creature (Path to Exile, Reality Shift, Beast Within), and those same three are the deck's entire instant-speed interaction.

Sixteen lands enter tapped (thirteen outright, plus three fetch lands that bring one in tapped), and three more — Mutavault, Reliquary Tower, Temple of the False God — are colourless in a three-colour deck. Shore Leave Planet looks like a fourth, but for {4}{U} it becomes a non-legendary copy of Spock until end of turn and can attack for a second reveal.
The Spacecraft half of the list wants creatures tapped for Station charge counters (6+ for Galileo, 16+ for Enterprise) and rarely gets there; Kirk's +3/+3 is the only payoff that comes online early.

The landfall shell is lopsided: ten cards pay off a land entering (Lotus Cobra, Scute Swarm, Tireless Tracker, Amanda Grayson, Chief Kyle, M'Ress, Syndicate Liquidators, Galileo, Enterprise, Farragut) and only Exploration adds a land drop, so those ten fire once a turn. The multiplier the list is missing is land drops, not more payoffs.

Spock triggers on entering as well as attacking, and the attack trigger happens before blockers, so he does not need to connect. The precon already blinks him: Chief Kyle on landfall, Temporal Tribulation and The Guardian of Forever at instant speed (which also protects him), Balance of Terror on chapters II and III, and Colossal Clone Master enters as a non-legendary second Spock whose power is your land-name count. Janice Rand and Guardian Project pay off each re-entry, and Brainstorm, Ponder and Augur of Autumn set or show the top card. What the list lacks is a blink that needs no land drop, mana or card.

Balance of Terror's chapters trigger before combat, so blinking Spock with it trades that turn's attack trigger for an end-step enter trigger. It's a real gain on Lt. Arex, Hornet Queen, T'Pring or a land, not on Spock himself.

Interaction and engine are separate problems, so they are costed separately here: the shared four fix removal in every direction, and the six direction cards are spent on one engine rather than six unrelated upgrades.

Win conditions (finishers in the 99, counted by the deck-comparison skill's rule): big threats — Planet Killer, Lt. Arex, Ever-Adapting, Colossal Clone Master, U.S.S. Defiant, Mirror Migrant, Syndicate Liquidators; armies and team evasion — Shuttlecraft Galileo, Scute Swarm, M'Ress, Crew Coordinator, Giant Space Amoeba.

core.name: Shared answers
core.description: Four cheap instants that go in every direction. Spot removal goes from three to six — all of it instant speed — and Counterspell stops a spell on the stack, which nothing in the list could do before.

swaps.why: One mana exiles any creature at instant speed, tied with Path to Exile as the cheapest answer in the deck. Planet Killer costs eight, must attack every combat if able, and does nothing the turn it lands.
Three mana destroys any permanent at instant speed, a second catch-all answer next to Beast Within. Command Chair is six mana, enters tapped and only ever ramps.

Split second kills an artifact or enchantment with no response, which matters against Equipment and Rhystic-style pieces. Giant Space Amoeba copies itself every time it attacks, but it never triggers Spock or landfall. Chief Montgomery Scott stays instead: his {6} ability puts Colossal Clone Master in as another Spock, or Lt. Arex for three cards and three lands.
Two mana stops the sweeper or the combo piece outright. Echo of Eons is a six-mana wheel that refills every opponent's hand too.

directions.name: Transporter Room
directions.pitch: The precon already makes Spock enter again — Chief Kyle, Temporal Tribulation, The Guardian of Forever and Colossal Clone Master — but each needs a land drop, mana or a card. Far Traveler gives him a free blink at every end step after he attacks, Starfield Vocalist makes every enter trigger happen twice, Gilraen and Momentary Blink blink at instant speed (which is also how this build protects him), Penance picks the card he reveals, and Hornet Queen is the free cast that gets better every time it re-enters. It folds if Spock is exiled while you're tapped out, and to effects that stop enter triggers.
directions.plays_like: Two to four Spock reveals a turn

how_to_play.summary: Attack with Spock, blink him at the end step, and let every re-entry reveal another free card.

sections.title: Turns 1–4
points: Far Traveler before Spock is the key start: from then on every attack is followed by an end-step blink, two triggers a turn for no mana.
Spend ramp on differently named lands — the free-cast ceiling is the name count, Colossal Clone Master needs six and Hornet Queen seven.
Hold Momentary Blink or {2} for Gilraen on the turn Spock lands; they are his protection as well as extra triggers.

sections.title: Turns 5–7
points: Attack with Spock every turn: the trigger fires on the attack, before blockers, and Far Traveler only blinks a creature that is tapped.
With a Spock trigger on the stack, use Penance to put your best expensive card on top. Colossal Clone Master is the best one: it enters as a second, non-legendary Spock.

With Far Traveler out, point Chief Kyle and Balance of Terror at Lt. Arex, Hornet Queen or T'Pring instead of Spock — a Spock exiled until the end step misses his own end-step blink, and Balance of Terror's chapters come before combat.
If Far Traveler is out, return Spock straight away with Gilraen: the vigilance counter from a delayed return means he no longer taps to attack.

sections.title: Closing
points: Spock and a Clone Master copy both attack, Spock blinks one of them at the end step, and Starfield Vocalist doubles that enter — three or four reveals a turn.
Order the end-step triggers so Far Traveler's blink resolves before a warped Starfield Vocalist is exiled, and the re-entry still triggers twice.
Against a board wipe, Temporal Tribulation exiles Spock and the Clone Master in response and both come back at the end step.

swaps.why: Spock gains 'at the beginning of your end step, blink a tapped creature you control', so every attack is followed by an enter trigger for no mana. It's a Background, but in the 99 it is a plain enchantment. Pike can tap two blockers for {2}, which Spock doesn't need: his trigger fires on the attack.

Every trigger caused by a permanent entering happens twice — Spock's reveal, Janice Rand's land, Guardian Project's draw and every landfall trigger in the deck. Tribble Cluster is a 1/1 that needs four combat steps to be worth a card.

Putting a card from your hand on top of your library costs no mana and works at instant speed, so before each Spock trigger resolves you choose what he reveals. Sam Kirk only investigates when an opponent casts a creature spell.

{2}, {T} blinks another creature at instant speed: the removal spell fizzles and Spock re-enters with a fresh trigger. S.S. Botany Bay is graveyard hate that needs eight charge counters before it even flies.
Two instant-speed blinks from one card, from hand and again with flashback, and each is a Spock trigger that also answers a removal spell. Merciful Mandate only untaps your team or ends one combat.

Free off Spock's trigger at seven land names, and every blink after that makes four more flying deathtouch Insects — eight with Starfield Vocalist. Scute Swarm only pays off land drops, which this direction doesn't add.

directions.win_conditions_note: The core trades Planet Killer and Giant Space Amoeba for interaction and this direction swaps Scute Swarm for Hornet Queen, leaving 7: within the 5–8 target.

directions.name: Land Engine
directions.pitch: Exploration, Loot, Wayward Swordtooth and Oracle of Mul Daya each add a land drop, and Spock, Janice Rand, Lt. Arex and Stable Wormhole put in more lands without one, so the eleven landfall payoffs fire several times a turn and Starfield Vocalist and Ancient Greenwarden double them. Warp Speed makes every land enter untapped, and Spock adds a free card every time he enters or attacks, re-entering through Far Traveler, Chief Kyle and Momentary Blink. It loses to a creature sweeper on a turn it can't rebuild: three of the four land-drop cards are creatures, so hold Heroic Intervention for that turn and rebuild with Exploration, Felidar Retreat and Multani.
directions.plays_like: Two or three land drops a turn, each one turned into bodies

how_to_play.summary: Play two or three lands a turn and let Rampaging Baloths, Scute Swarm, M'Ress and Felidar Retreat turn each one into bodies, then attack behind Felidar Retreat's counters or Shuttlecraft Galileo's flying, with Multani and Lt. Arex as the big tramplers.

sections.title: Turns 1–3
points: Get an extra land drop down early: Exploration on turn one, Loot or Wayward Swordtooth on turn three (turn two after Exploration or Sol Ring), Oracle of Mul Daya on four. Each one is another land a turn and another round of landfall triggers. Wayward Swordtooth can't attack or block until you control ten permanents, so don't count on it as a blocker early.

Ramp into new land names: Farseek and Nature's Lore can fetch typed duals such as Canopy Vista or Sodden Verdure, and Rampant Growth and Cultivate should take a basic type you don't have yet. Each new name raises Spock's free-cast ceiling.
Use every land drop; spare lands in hand still get played later, because Lt. Arex, Growth Spiral and a kicked Joint Exploration put them onto the battlefield.

Warp Speed on turn three makes every later land enter untapped; its search can take Shore Leave Planet instead of a basic. Dreamroot Cascade, Overgrown Farmland and Deserted Beach enter untapped from your third land anyway, so play them after your first two.

sections.title: Turns 4–6
points: With two of Exploration, Loot, Wayward Swordtooth and Oracle of Mul Daya out you play three lands a turn. With Oracle out, play the land on top first and check the new top card; crack fetch lands last, because the shuffle throws away a top card you set up for Spock.

Mole Man and Ancient Greenwarden let you play lands from your graveyard: crack a fetch land, then spend an extra land drop replaying it for two more landfall triggers. Greenwarden also makes every landfall trigger happen twice.

Colossal Clone Master is best as a second Spock: the copy isn't legendary, its power is your land-name count, and it reveals when it enters and attacks. It isn't your commander, so Janice Rand and Far Traveler don't work on it. Copy Rampaging Baloths instead when you need bodies.
Tap two lands for mana, then cast Temporal Tribulation on them: they come back at your end step as two more landfall triggers, and flashback does it again.
Balance of Terror's chapters II and III come before combat, so blink Lt. Arex (three cards and up to three lands), Sun Titan or a land with them, not Spock.

Your answers are instants: Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Reality Shift, Stroke of Midnight, Generous Gift, Beast Within, Krosan Grip and Counterspell. Celebrate the Mountain-king exiles a nonland permanent from each opponent, two each with Starfield Vocalist out.

sections.title: Spock's enter trigger
points: Whenever Spock enters or attacks he reveals the top card: you may cast it free if its mana value is at most the number of differently named lands you control, a land can go onto the battlefield (tapped, unless Warp Speed is out), and anything left on top you draw. Janice Rand puts in another land each time.

Know the top card before he triggers: Oracle of Mul Daya and Augur of Autumn show it, and Brainstorm, Ponder and Joint Exploration set it. Joint Exploration before attacks: scry 2 to put the card you want him to reveal second, draw the first, and he reveals that one.
With Janice Rand out, let Spock's reveal resolve first: Janice moves the cards above her land to the bottom, so the top card you set up would be gone.

Far Traveler blinks a tapped creature at your end step: after Spock attacks, blink him for a second reveal and another Janice Rand land, or blink Lt. Arex after he attacks for three more cards. Without Far Traveler, play your extra lands after combat so Chief Kyle blinks Spock once he has attacked; with it, point Kyle at other creatures, because a Spock in exile at the end step misses his own blink.

Starfield Vocalist makes every enter and landfall trigger happen twice; warp it for {1}{U} on the turn that matters most, and stack the end-step blinks above its exile trigger so the returning Spock still gets doubled.

Momentary Blink and Temporal Tribulation are instants, so hold one for the removal spell aimed at Spock. Chief Montgomery Scott's {6} ability works at instant speed too: at the end of an opponent's turn, put Colossal Clone Master in as another Spock, or Lt. Arex for three cards and up to three lands.

sections.title: Closing
points: Rampaging Baloths with two extra land drops makes three 4/4 Beasts a turn, and Spock, Janice Rand and Stable Wormhole add more; Starfield Vocalist or Ancient Greenwarden doubles each one.

Felidar Retreat makes a 2/2 Cat per land when you are behind and puts a +1/+1 counter on the whole team when the board is stable. It is an enchantment, so it survives Wrath of God and rebuilds the army.
Shuttlecraft Galileo is the evasion: tap two 4/4 Beasts (at sorcery speed) to station it to 6, and from then on each time it attacks, up to seven attackers gain flying. Captain Kirk gives it +3/+3.

Multani counts every land you control and every land card in your graveyard, so cracked fetch lands and cycled duals grow it; if it dies, pay {1}{G} and return two lands to hand to put it back in your hand, then replay them for more landfall. Lt. Arex tramples for your land-name count.
Late on, Warp Speed's draw-two costs {X} less where X is your land names, so at seven or more names it is {U}{U} and a sacrifice.

A creature sweeper on a turn you can't rebuild is how this loses: Loot, Wayward Swordtooth, Oracle of Mul Daya and every payoff creature die together. Hold Heroic Intervention for it, and keep Exploration and Felidar Retreat, which survive it.

swaps.why: One extra land drop every turn, and once the land count catches up his second ability puts a creature from the top six straight onto the battlefield. Pike only taps or untaps two other creatures.
Two extra land drops turns every landfall trigger in the deck into three a turn. Tribble Cluster is a 1/1 that needs four combat steps before it is worth a card.

An extra land drop for three mana with a 5/5 body attached — the city's blessing (ten permanents) only gates attacking and blocking; the land drop works from turn three. Sam Kirk only investigates when an opponent casts a creature spell, one Clue at a time.

Enabler and payoff in one card: lands played from the graveyard bring fetches back for a second trigger, and every land still makes a Moloid. S.S. Botany Bay is graveyard hate that needs eight charge counters before it even flies.

Every land that enters makes a 2/2 Cat, or puts a +1/+1 counter on the whole team when the board is stable, and as an enchantment it survives creature sweepers. Merciful Mandate only untaps your team or ends one combat.

A 6/6 trampler that makes a 4/4 Beast whenever a land enters, two or three a turn with the extra land drops. Christine Chapel is a four-mana 2/2 that only grows when you gain life. Balance of Terror stays: its chapters II and III blink Lt. Arex, Sun Titan or a land for more landfall.

Spock gains 'at the beginning of your end step, blink a tapped creature you control': every attack is followed by a second Spock trigger and another land from Janice Rand, for no mana. It's a Background, but in the 99 it is a plain enchantment. Uhura spends {4} and a tap every turn on a random instant or sorcery from an opponent's library.

Every trigger caused by a permanent entering happens twice: all eleven landfall payoffs, Spock's reveal and Janice Rand's land when he enters, and the enter triggers of Lt. Arex and Celebrate the Mountain-king. Doubling the payoffs beats adding one more, and Syndicate Liquidators is a five-mana copy of what Amanda Grayson does for four.

Two instant-speed blinks from one card, from hand and again with flashback: each is a Spock reveal and a Janice Rand land, and each answers a removal spell aimed at him. McCoy is a five-mana 0/4 whose team-wide counter happens once.

Every land enters untapped — the ten lands that always enter tapped, and every land Spock, Janice Rand, Lt. Arex, Stable Wormhole, the ramp spells and the fetch lands put in tapped — so each extra land drop is mana the same turn. It also finds a basic or Shore Leave Planet, which was Cold-Blooded Crew's main job through landcycling; otherwise the Crew is a six-mana 4/4.
Green-blue that enters untapped once you control two other lands. Earth always enters tapped and only gains 1 life; Shore Leave Planet is still there for Warp Speed's Planet search.
Green-white that enters untapped once you control two other lands. Risa always enters tapped and only gains 1 life.
White-blue that enters untapped once you control two other lands. Vulcan always enters tapped and only gains 1 life.

Two mana at instant speed: scry 2, then draw a card, so you know and partly choose what Spock reveals on his next trigger. Kicked for {G} more, it also puts a land from your hand onto the battlefield. The Guardian of Forever's {4} ability sacrifices Spock and returns him at the end step, one extra Spock trigger for four mana; The Command Zone's and TCGplayer's upgrade lists both cut it.

directions.win_conditions_note: The core trades Planet Killer and Giant Space Amoeba for interaction, and Starfield Vocalist replaces Syndicate Liquidators; Felidar Retreat and Rampaging Baloths turn land drops into an army instead. The 2026-11-18 review swaps add Multani as a ninth finisher, so decks/landing-party.md is back at the stock count of 9.

directions.name: More Worlds
directions.pitch: Push the resource Spock actually counts: 43 lands and 38 different names, cutting the three colourless lands that were doing nothing in a three-colour deck. Shore Leave Planet stays, because for {4}{U} it attacks as a second Spock. Cheapest direction and the most direct upgrade to the commander, but it adds no engine.

how_to_play.summary: Trade clunky permanents for lands, then let the name count carry Spock.

sections.title: Turns 1–3
points: Play the untapped duals first (Brushland, Adarkar Wastes, Yavimaya Coast) so the name count grows without costing tempo; the pain is one life per coloured use.
Keep the four Forest, two Island, two Plains for Rampant Growth, Cultivate and Kirk to find.

sections.title: Turns 4–6
points: Every new name raises Spock's free-cast ceiling, so a six-drop on top becomes castable at six lands rather than eight.
Exploration plus 43 lands means two drops a turn is normal; do not be shy about playing lands you do not immediately need.

sections.title: Closing
points: At 38 names Spock casts almost anything on top for free; attack with him every turn to trigger it twice per round.
With spare mana, make Shore Leave Planet a copy of Spock before combat and attack with both. It stops being a land for that turn, so the name count drops by one.
You are at 43 lands with eight basics — keep two spare lands in hand for Exploration turns, and check your remaining basics before cracking Evolving Wilds.

swaps.why: An untapped green-white source with a new name for one life per coloured use. Temple of the False God is colourless and only taps once you control five lands.
Untapped white-blue fixing and a brand-new name. Mutavault is a colourless 2/2 that does not help you cast anything; this direction trades it up.
Untapped green-blue fixing and a new name. Reliquary Tower is colourless and only lifts the hand-size limit, which a 43-land deck rarely needs.
Trades a 0/6 that only taps or untaps creatures for a land that enters untapped early and adds a name. The deck goes to 43 lands, so every drop matters.
A white-blue fast land with a new name instead of a 1/1 that needs four combat steps before it is a real threat.
Green-white fixing and a new name for a 3/3 that only investigates when an opponent casts a creature spell.

directions.win_conditions_note: Only lands and cheap utility change after the core trades Planet Killer and Giant Space Amoeba for interaction, leaving 7: within the 5–8 target.

recommendation: Take Land Engine (picked). After the review it cuts only cards that do nothing for either engine, so it keeps the pieces that make Spock enter again — Chief Kyle, Temporal Tribulation, Balance of Terror and Colossal Clone Master — and adds four land-drop enablers that keep working when Spock is answered. The seven extra swaps cost about €4.60: Far Traveler and Momentary Blink turn Spock's enter trigger into extra lands through Janice Rand, Starfield Vocalist doubles both, and Warp Speed with three slow lands makes those lands usable mana the turn they enter. One swap is still to buy: Joint Exploration for The Guardian of Forever. Transporter Room is the stronger Spock-only build at about €9 if you want to push the blink side later; More Worlds is the cheapest and the safest mana base, but it adds no engine.

bracket3.name: Bracket 3 package
bracket3.rule: Bracket 3 (Upgraded) allows up to three Game Changers, no mass land denial, no chained extra turns, and game-ending two-card combos only late in the game.
bracket3.description: Landing Party at bracket 3 means more land drops, a card for every land, a known top card for Spock's free casts, and a way to end the game with the army the lands make.
notes: Spock casts the top card for free when its mana value is no more than your number of differently named lands. By the mid-game Avenger of Zendikar and Overwhelming Stampede are free off the top, and Captain Pike and Oracle of Mul Daya show you the top card first.
Wrath of God comes out, which leaves Austere Command as the only board wipe. That suits a deck that wins with its own army, but it is one fewer reset if you fall behind.

Changed on 2026-11-15: Genesis Device replaced Springheart Nantuko. After your CardTrader order (Warp Speed, three slow lands, Stable Wormhole and the three Land Engine extras) went into the deck, two cuts changed: Crop Rotation now replaces Sulu and Avenger of Zendikar replaces Captain Kirk.
Changed on 2026-11-15 after comparing with The Command Zone's upgrade list (episode 773): Planar Genesis replaced Kellan, the Kid, which added one more side theme where a lands card fits better.

swaps.why: Game Changer. One mana at instant speed trades a land for any land in your library. It is a landfall trigger on an opponent's turn and a new land name for Spock, and it fetches Field of the Dead if you add it. Sulu is a 3/3 that explores when it taps; the deck now has better three-drops.
Draw a card and gain 1 life for every land that enters. With Exploration, Azusa or Loot that is three or four cards a turn, every turn. In 47% of Spock decks.

You may look at the top card of your library at any time and play lands from the top, so you know what Spock will reveal and can play a land out of the way first. Its power and toughness equal your number of differently named lands. T'Pring (23%) is a one-off fight.
An extra land drop every turn, lands playable from the top of your library, and the top card always revealed: more land drops and the top-card knowledge Spock needs.

Another extra land drop, and every creature that enters explores: a land goes to your hand, anything else gives the creature a +1/+1 counter. Tokens from M'Ress, Scute Swarm and Felidar Retreat explore too. Chief Scott's ability costs six mana.

Two mana at instant speed: look at the top four cards and put a land from them onto the battlefield, or take one card into your hand. It is a landfall trigger on any player's turn and it finds the land or the spell you need. Starfleet Communicator draws nothing until two creatures each carry one.

Three mana: it enters and puts a basic land or Shore Leave Planet onto the battlefield, which is a landfall trigger. Later, for {3}{G}{G} at sorcery speed, you sacrifice it and any number of lands and fetch that many lands: every landfall card you control triggers once per land, and you can fetch all different names. U.S.S. Farragut costs six and the creature it puts out goes back to your library.

A 0/1 Plant for each land you control, then every land puts a +1/+1 counter on every Plant. Seven mana, or free off the top with Spock. Captain Kirk finds one basic land each time he attacks, which Tatyova and the extra land drops now do better.

Until end of turn your creatures get +X/+X and trample, where X is the greatest power among them. With a board of Officers, Insects and Beasts it ends the game, and Spock can cast it for free. Wrath of God destroys your own army.

A new land name that later sacrifices itself for a Forest and a Plains: two landfall triggers, and it can fetch Canopy Vista, Scattered Groves or Irrigated Farmland. Temple of the False God makes no mana until you control five lands.

premium.why: Game Changer. Once you control seven differently named lands, every land that enters also makes a 2/2 Zombie. This deck is built on different land names, so it turns land drops into an army with no other card needed. Crop Rotation fetches it.

deck_changes.why: Whenever you attack it creates a tapped Planet land token that taps for any colour: a landfall trigger every combat, ramp, and one new land name (New Planet) for Spock. Satyr Wayfinder is a 1/1 that finds one land, in 17% of Spock decks.

The only Azusa moves to World Shaper, which gets cards first. Ka-Zar comes from the Bulk pile: you may look at the top card any time and play lands from it, which also shows what Spock will reveal, and Zabu grows with every land. Five mana instead of three, so buy a second Azusa later to swap back.

An extra land drop every turn, and you play lands straight off the top of your library, which stays revealed: you always know what Spock will reveal, and playing the top land digs him toward a spell. It took over from Ka-Zar, which showed the top card for five mana but added no land drop.
Instant removal for any nonland permanent: spot removal was the one category below target. Jefferies Tube's activations cost {2}-{4} plus a tap.

The deck's biggest single threat: +1/+1 for each land you control and each land card in your graveyard, with reach and trample, and for {1}{G} and two lands returned to hand (which you then replay) it returns from your graveyard to your hand. Farragut is a 6-mana landfall payoff that isn't a creature until 7 charge counters.
Four mana exiles a nonland permanent from each opponent, and Starfield Vocalist makes it two from each; recruit also loots a card. T'Pring was a 5-mana fight that needs a big enough creature.
